newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf Coast attracting West African barrels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf Coast attracting West African barrels.

text.p: The U.S. Gulf Coast continued to attract various offers for West African crude cargoes on Friday, while North Sea offers remained scant, traders said.
Several companies were showing Qua Iboe, Forcadoes, Cabinda and other West African grades for arrival on the Gulf Coast from around mid-March to early April, traders said.
Talk focused on efforts to co-load Cabinda, Nemba and Qua Iboe for the Gulf Coast, traders said.
The Qua Iboe cargoes were going for a premium of around $2.10-15 a barrel to Dated Brent, traders said.
One East Coast trader noted that Far East demand for West African crudes has "slackened off a bit," increasing Gulf Coast availabilities.
The scarcity of North Sea offers reflects the narrow transatlantic arbitrage, although there were signs that the window may have cracked open for a few players, traders said.
The spread between bellwethers West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent for April was at $1.60-65 a barrel Friday afternoon, up about five cents from the high on Thursday afternoon.
Meanwhile, Dated Brent fell to a 20-cent discount to March for late February, traders said.
A U.S. major bought Forties loading March 3-5, March 6-8 and March 11-13 for Dated Brent plus 40-44 cents, traders said.
A cargo of Norwegian Heidrun crude was on offer, although the timing was unclear.
Separately, traders in London noted that European sour markets have softened under the pressure of fresh Iraqi spot volumes and plentiful supplies of other sour grades.
Iraq is selling extra spot cargoes to make up for a shortfall in revenue under the U.N. oil-for-food deal as a result of falling world oil prices.
In Latin America, Bolivia's state-owned oil company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) sold 250,000 barrels of 45-API gravity reconstituted crude oil to a U.S. domestic refiner.
The crude was sold at a discount of around $4.79 a barrel to WTI/Cushing.
The crude loads February 24-25 at the Chilean port of Arica.
Elsewhere, a U.S. refiner was still offering a prompt Vasconia cargo for around WTI minus $2.30 a barrel, while Colombian state-owned Ecopetrol is showing a Cano Limon.
